teachingSections.title: Upper and Lower Egypt
teachingSections.where: Read the assigned OER PDF, pages 4, 7.
teach: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea. Upper Egypt is in the south, upstream. Lower Egypt is in the north, downstream, near the Nile Delta.
A delta is land deposited at a river’s mouth. The Nile Delta lies in the north. Cataracts are rocky rapids farther upstream that can make boat travel difficult.
Upper and Lower describe positions along the river. They do not mean top and bottom on a page. Follow the river toward its mouth to move downstream.
Remember the pair: Upper Egypt = south and upstream; Lower Egypt = north and downstream, near the delta.

example.prompt: A traveler follows the Nile north toward the delta. Which part of Egypt is the traveler approaching?
example.thinking: North follows the river downstream toward its mouth. Lower Egypt is the downstream region.
example.why: The region is named for its downstream position, even though it appears above Upper Egypt on a north-up map.

teachingSections.tryPrompt: Which pair correctly describes Upper Egypt?
teachingSections.tryAnswer: South and upstream. Upper Egypt was farther upstream, even though it appears lower on a north-up map.

connections.prompt: How does the Nile’s flow explain the name Lower Egypt?
options: Lower Egypt is downstream, toward the northern delta.
Lower Egypt is upstream, toward the southern source.
Lower Egypt is named for its position at a page’s bottom.
connections.rationale: Lower Egypt is downstream, toward the northern delta. The Nile flows north. Next, connect its water and silt to farming.

connections.prompt: A different river flows south. Which rule still works when describing its course?
options: Downstream follows the water toward its mouth.
Downstream must always mean north on any river.
Downstream always means the tallest land nearby.
connections.rationale: Downstream follows the water toward its mouth. Read river directions on a modern map. Upstream and downstream follow water flow; they do not always match north and south.

vocabulary.definition: Rocky river rapids that make travel difficult.
vocabulary.example: A boat must unload beside rough rocky water.
vocabulary.nonExample: A cataract is not the river’s mouth.

vocabulary.definition: Land built from sediment at a river’s mouth, often with branching channels.
vocabulary.example: The Nile Delta is near the Mediterranean Sea.
vocabulary.nonExample: A delta is not an upstream rocky rapid.
